Attack is the type of payload combinations to perform
batteringram the same payload into all defined payload positions at once, pitchfork combines multiple payload sets and clusterbomb generates permutations and combinations for all payloads
Example: 
```yaml
- attack: clusterbomb
```
Note: this is only applicable when 'payloads' are defined

```yaml
- body: "key=value&key2=value2"
```

digest-username.markdownDescription:

Example: 
```yaml
- digest-username: admin
```

```yaml
- disable-cookie: true
```

DisablePathAutomerge disables the automatic merging of path/query-params from input/target to path defined in template
Example: 
```yaml
- disable-path-automerge: true
```
disable-path-automerge.title: disable auto merging of path

extractors.title: extractors to run on response

Fuzzing or DAST specifies rules for fuzzing requests
these rules mutate the input request to generate multiple requests
For example, replacing all query param values with sqli payloads
fuzzing.title: fuzzin rules for http fuzzing

headers.markdownDescription:

```yaml
- headers:
	User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
```
headers.title: headers to send with the http request

host-redirects.markdownDescription:
HostRedirects specifies whether only redirects to the same host should be followed by the HTTP Client
When set to true, only redirects to the same host are followed
Example: 
```yaml
- host-redirects: true
```
host-redirects.title: follow same host http redirects

Optional ID of this HTTP Request Block
This is useful when calling /executing this request block in flow
By default, current index in the http array is used as ID

```yaml
- id: wp-login
```
id.title: id for the http request

iterate-all.title: iterate all the values

max-redirects.markdownDescription:

```yaml
- max-redirects: 10
```
max-redirects.title: maximum number of redirects to follow

max-size.markdownDescription:
MaxSize is the maximum size of the response body to be read
Example: 
```yaml
- max-size: 1024
```

method.markdownDescription:


Name is the optional name of the request
If a name is specified, all the named request in a template can be matched upon
in a combined manner allowing multi-request based matchers.
name.title: name for the http request

path.markdownDescription:
Path contains HTTP URL[s] to be sent. Here only Path portion is generally specified and host is templatetized
Example: 
```yaml
- path:
	{{BaseURL}}/admin
```
path.title: path(s) for the http request

# inline payloads
	username:
		- admin
		- root
	password:
		- password
		- admin

  # file payloads
	username: /path/to/usernames.txt
	password: /path/to/passwords.txt
payloads.markdownDescription:
Payloads contains key-value pairs of payloads to be used
These payloads when referenced in http request will be iterated appropriately and replaced
Optionally payload also support loading values from file instead of defining them inline
Example: 
```yaml
- payloads:
	username:
		- admin
		- root
	password:
		- password
		- admin
```
payloads.title: payloads for the http request

pipeline.markdownDescription:
Pipeline defines if the attack should be performed with HTTP 1.1 Pipelining
All requests must be idempotent (GET/POST). This can be used for race conditions/billions requests.
Example: 
```yaml
- pipeline: true
```
pipeline.title: perform HTTP 1.1 pipelining

pipeline-concurrent-connections.markdownDescription:
PipelineConcurrentConnections specifies the number of concurrent connections to be used for pipelining
Example: 
```yaml
- pipeline-concurrent-connections: 10
  pipeline: true
```
pipeline-concurrent-connections.title: number of pipelining connections

pipeline-requests-per-connection.markdownDescription:
PipelineRequestsPerConnection specifies the number of requests to be sent per connection
Example: 
```yaml
- pipeline: true
  pipeline-requests-per-connection: 10
```
pipeline-requests-per-connection.title: number of requests to send per pipelining connections

examples:
# has query params
	- type: dsl
		dsl:
			- 'len(query) > 0'

 # has request body
	- type: dsl
		dsl:
			- 'len(body) > 0'

 # has post method
	- type: dsl
		dsl:
			- 'method == "POST"'

 # has post method and body
	- type: dsl
		dsl:
			- 'method == "POST"'
			- 'len(body) > 0'
		condition: and
pre-condition.markdownDescription:
Pre-condition is only applicable for fuzzing/DAST requests and specifies whether fuzzing should run on this input
It is a twin of matchers and can express pre-conditions that must be met before fuzzing
Example: 
```yaml
- pre-condition:
	- type: dsl
		dsl:
			- 'len(query) > 0'
```
With this pre-condition only inputs that have query params will be fuzzed by this template
pre-condition.title: pre-condition for fuzzing/dast

pre-condition-operator.markdownDescription:
Pre-condition-operator specifies the condition used for combining multiple pre-conditions
By default, it is OR
Example: 
```yaml
- pre-condition-operator: and
```
pre-condition-operator.title: condition between the filters

protocol-redirects.markdownDescription: Specifies whether only same-protocol redirects should be followed by the HTTP Client
protocol-redirects.title: follow same protocol http redirects

race.markdownDescription:
Race determines if all the request have to be attempted at the same time (Race Condition)
The actual number of requests that will be sent is determined by the `race_count`  field.
Example: 
```yaml
- race: true
  race_count: 100
```
race.title: perform race-http request coordination attack

race_count.markdownDescription:
RaceCount specifies the number of requests to be sent when attempting race condition attacks
Example: 
```yaml
- race: true
  race_count: 100
```
race_count.title: number of times to repeat request in race condition

examples:
# raw-get-request
	- |

		Host: {{Hostname}}


# raw-post-request
	- |
		POST / HTTP/1.1
		Host: {{Hostname}}
		Content-Type: application/json
		Content-Length: 13


		{"key": "value"}
raw.markdownDescription:
Raw contains HTTP Request[s] in raw or request dump format

	- |
		GET / HTTP/1.1
		Host: {{Hostname}}

read-all.markdownDescription:
Enables force reading of the entire raw unsafe request body ignoring  any specified content length headers
Example: 
```yaml
- read-all: true
```
read-all.title: force read all body

redirects.markdownDescription:
Redirects specifies whether to follow redirects or not
This can be use in conjunction with max-redirects to effectively control the redirects
Example: 
```yaml
- redirects: true
```
redirects.title: follow http redirects

req-condition.markdownDescription: Deprecated: this is automatically identified and used (https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei/issues/2393)
req-condition.title: preserve request history

self-contained.markdownDescription:
SelfContained specifies whether the request is self-contained or not
This means if the request is dependent on input or is self-contained
Example: 
```yaml

```

signature.markdownDescription: Signature is the HTTP Request signature Method

skip-secret-file.markdownDescription: Skips the authentication or authorization configured in the secret file
skip-secret-file.title: bypass secret file

skip-variables-check.markdownDescription:
SkipVariablesCheck skips the check for unresolved variables in request
This is also useful in case where body contains payload in format of {{xyz}}
Example: 
```yaml
- skip-variables-check: true
```
skip-variables-check.title: skip variable checks

stop-at-first-match.markdownDescription:
StopAtFirstMatch specifies whether to stop at first match or not
This is useful for cases like brute-forcing where we want to stop once we find the first correct login credential
Example: 
```yaml
- stop-at-first-match: true
```
stop-at-first-match.title: stop at first match

threads.markdownDescription:
Threads specifies concurreny with which requests should be sent
It should not be specified unless explicitly behaviour and its value is obtained from -pc (-payload-concurrency) flag
Example: 
```yaml
- threads: 10
```
threads.title: threads for sending requests

unsafe.markdownDescription:
Unsafe specifies whether to use rawhttp engine for sending Non RFC-Compliant requests.
This uses the [rawhttp](https://github.com/projectdiscovery/rawhttp) engine to achieve complete
control over the request, with no normalization performed by the client.
Example: 
```yaml
- unsafe: true
```
unsafe.title: use rawhttp non-strict-rfc client

code.markdownDescription:
Code protocol block for executing external engines (python, sh, etc.)
Example:
```yaml
code:
  - engine:
      - py
    source: |
      print("hello")
```
code.title: code snippets to make

constants.markdownDescription:
Constants are the global constants that once defined here can be used anywhere in the template
It can be used in same way as variables but only difference is that constants cannot be overridden by -V flag at runtime
Example: 
```yaml
constants:
  exploit: 'x0x0x0x0x0x0x'
```
constants.title: constant for the template

dns.markdownDescription:
DNS protocol block for sending DNS queries
Example:
```yaml
dns:
  - name: "{{FQDN}}"
    type: A
    matchers:
      - type: word
        words:
          - "IN\tA"
```
dns.title: dns requests to make

file.markdownDescription:
File protocol block for matching against local files
Example:
```yaml
file:
  - extensions:
      - all
```
file.title: file requests to make

examples:
| # example-vhost-enum
	ssl(); // ->  execute all ssl protocol requests
	dns(); // ->  execute all dns protocol requests
	for (let got of template.domains) { // ->  iterate over 'domains' array variable
		set('vhost', got); // ->  set 'vhost' variable to current domain
		http(); // ->  execute all http protocol requests
	}
flow.markdownDescription:
Flow describes how multiple request-blocks/protocols should be combined together and executed
It is a javascript code where each protocol is a function and all request-blocks are indexed by their corresponding index in request array
Example: 
 flow: http(1) && http(2)
 means that second http request will be executed only if first http request is successful (aka matched)
flow.title: template execution flow in js

headless.markdownDescription:
Headless protocol block for browser automation
Example:
```yaml
headless:
  - steps:
      - action: navigate
        args:
          url: "{{BaseURL}}"
```
headless.title: headless requests to make

examples:
# http get
	- method: GET
		path:
			- "{{BaseURL}}"
		
		matchers:
			- type: status
				status:
					- 200

# raw get
	- raw:
			- |
					GET HTTP/1.1
					Host: {{Hostname}}
				
			matchers:
			- type: status
				status:
					- 200

# http self contained
	- method: GET
		path:
		  - "https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges"
		
		self-contained: true
		headers:
			Authorization: 'Basic {{base64(token)}}'
		
		matchers:
		  - type: word
		    part: body
		    words:
		      - '"object":'
		      - '"url":'
		      - '"data":'
		    condition: and
http.markdownDescription:
HTTP is the protocol block for sending HTTP requests
It is of array type and can contain multiple requests
Example: 
```yaml
http: 
	- method: GET
		path:
			- "{{BaseURL}}"
		
		matchers:
			- type: status
			status:
				- 200
```
http.title: http requests to make

id.markdownDescription:
ID is the unique id for the template.
 ### Good IDs 
A good ID uniquely identifies what the requests in the template
are doing. Let's say you have a template that identifies a git-config
file on the webservers, a good name would be `git-config-exposure`. Another
example name is `azure-apps-nxdomain-takeover`
id.title: id of the template

info.markdownDescription:
Info contains the required metadata information about the template
It is meant to provide basic but necessary info like name, author , severity
along with many other optional fields like metadata, classification etc
Example: 
```yaml
info: 
	name: Example Template
	author: pdteam
	severity: info
	description: This is an example template
```

Note: - 
For a template to be valid name,author,severity of `info` section must be set
info.title: info for the template

requests.markdownDescription:
HTTP is the protocol block for sending HTTP requests
It is of array type and can contain multiple requests
Example: 
```yaml
requests: 
	- method: GET
		path:
			- "{{BaseURL}}"
		
		matchers:
			- type: status
			status:
				- 200
```
requests.title: http requests to make

self-contained.markdownDescription:
Self-contained marks all requests in this template as independent of input which means input/target is not required for execution of template
but other variables defined in template need to be explicitly set using -V flag
Default value is false
Note: self-contained templates only run once regardless of how many targets where provided to nuclei
Example: 
```yaml
self-contained: true
```
Full example template of self-contained is available at https://cloud.projectdiscovery.io/public/aws-app-enum
self-contained.title: mark requests as self-contained

signature.markdownDescription: Signature is the HTTP Request signature Method
signature.title: signature is the http request signature method

ssl.markdownDescription:
SSL protocol block for TLS certificate / cipher checks
Example:
```yaml
ssl:
  - address: "{{Host}}:{{Port}}"
```
ssl.title: ssl requests to make

stop-at-first-match.markdownDescription:
stop-at-first-match stops the execution of template as soon as first match/result was found in a template given that template was sending multiple requests
this is required in case of default-login , brute-force and even detection templates where multiple requests are sent from template but we want to exit as soon as first match/result was found
Example: 
```yaml
stop-at-first-match: true
```
Full example template of stop-at-first-match is available at https://cloud.projectdiscovery.io/public/bitbucket-public-repository
stop-at-first-match.title: stop at first match

tcp.markdownDescription:
TCP/network protocol block for raw socket requests
Example:
```yaml
tcp:
  - host:
      - "{{Hostname}}"
    inputs:
      - data: "\n"
```
tcp.title: network(tcp) requests to make

variables.markdownDescription:
Variables are the global variables that once defined here can be used anywhere in the template
Variables are evaluated in the order they are defined so one variable can be referenced in another variable
Variables are evaluated before sending every requests so one can reference any variables that are available at runtime and they will be evaluate and used when referenced
Example: 
```yaml
variables:
  oast: {{interact-sh}}
  payload: "{{base64(oast)}}"
```
Full example template of variables is available at https://cloud.projectdiscovery.io/public/screenshot
Note: -
These variables can be overridden by -V flag at runtime if needed
variables.title: variables for the http request
